title: Trek Domane SL5 Review - 6 Months Later (best first road bike?)

takeaways.text: Very comfortable: he rides 100 km without back pain, helped by the rear IsoSpeed decoupler; comfortable enough that he slammed the stem.
The stock tires were poor; switching to 28 mm Pirelli P Zero Race TLR was the best-value upgrade, followed by carbon wheels.
In-frame storage is the feature he values most; internal routing does not bother him because a mechanic services the bike.
He paid about US$3,500 for the 105 mechanical SL 5; the SL 6 adds 105 Di2 and better wheels for about US$1,200 more.
Cons: 105 at this price, on the heavy side because of IsoSpeed and storage, bar tape wearing quickly, a top-frame plug that fell out, and a seatpost that slipped down even when tightened fully.

disclosure: The owner bought the bike himself; the description may carry affiliate links.
summary: An owner's six-month, 1,500 km review of a Trek Domane SL 5 Gen 4 bought as his first road bike.
